fix(incremental): include CSS source in dependency hash to prevent stale cache hits (#17704)

CSS modules have empty `code` in Vite's prerender bundle because their
content is extracted into separate assets. The incremental build's
`hashModules()` was hashing only the (empty) bundle code, so CSS edits
never changed the dependency hash and cached pages kept referencing
stale CSS filenames.

When a module's code is empty and its ID matches a CSS file pattern,
read the source file from disk and hash its contents instead." (#17705)

note: See the header of nested-ternaries-history.cjs. Events and diff sizes come from line-matched constructs, not from reading the commits: a construct is matched within its enclosing function by its tests, so a rename of the function, a moved construct or a rewritten test reads as removed plus introduced. Diff sizes count -U0 hunk lines inside the construct's new range, including reformatting. The bug-fix heuristic is length-history.cjs's isBugFix (precision and miss rate in `heuristic`). Regressions are associations, not effects.

diffsize.note: Non-mass commits only. `added` and `removed` are -U0 hunk lines inside the construct's range in the new version (removed: the old lines those hunks replace, so a rewritten line counts once as removed and once as added). pureInsertion: no existing line changed. The comparison is between different code in different commits, not the same change written two ways, and a formatter (Prettier in most of these repos) decides how a ternary chain is laid out.

heuristic.note: heuristicFixes.weightedYesShare is the heuristic's precision; heuristicOthers.weightedYesShare is the share of real fixes it misses among the commits it doesn't call fixes. One rater (a Claude subagent), reading messages and file lists only.

eventCheck.note: Hand input, one rater (the Claude model that ran nested-ternaries-history.cjs). The sample (out/nested-ternaries/history/event-sample.json, seed 20261111, up to three non-mass events per kind) has 78 events; these are the 55 that were read, chosen to cover every ternary kind and the conversion kinds of else-if chains (the else-if introduced/extended/removed kinds were checked more lightly). Each verdict compares the event's label with the commit's diff: correct, partly (the direction is right but the kind or the construct is off), wrong.
